senses.gloss:
Ghora Āṅgirasa
(‘the terrible descendant of the [sage] अङ्गिरस्’)
------------------------------------------
The Chāndogya Upaniṣad (3.17.6) while dealing with puruṣayajña (human life contemplated upon as a sacrifice) has mentioned that the sage घोर आङ्गिरस taught this science to कृष्ण Devakīputra. It is well-known from the Viṣṇupurāṇa (5.21.19) and the Bhāgavata (10.45.31) that सान्दीपनि of अवन्ति was the teacher of कृष्ण (and बलराम). The question is whether the two sages were one and the same.
Ghora was one of the eight sons of the sage अङ्गिरस्. Hence he was known as ‘Ghora-Āṅgirasa’. (Āṅgirasa = a descendant of अङ्गिरस्.) If सान्दीपनि belonged to the अङ्गिरस् गोत्र (lineage) and had the appellation ‘ghora’ (‘the terrible’) since he was a strict disciplinarian, the two sages can be deemed as one and the same person. But there is no clinching evidence to prove it.
